sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 'Unpublished Field Materials: Languages: Jukunoid' (JkOP.htm) and 'Endangered Jukunoid languages' (ELJkdOP.htm), rogerblench.info; Common Crawl 2024-02 and Wayback 2008/2015/2025 captures; whole-site Wayback CDX listings
sources.note: Pages list only Jibu dictionary, Kuteb grammar (Koops) and Kuteb photos. Wayback CDX of the entire site (receipts/) shows no file for Bete (Nigeria) or 'sounds of Bete' ever captured; the only 'Bete' paths are Côte d'Ivoire Bété artefact photos.

sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive work for Bete (0 grammar/sketch/phonology refs); Prischnegg 2008 tagged for byf only as 'comments on subclassification'.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project (ELCat), 'Bete' (ELP id 4018), Wayback capture 2025-01-19
sources.note: Sources listed: Dimmendaal & Voeltz 2007 (Routledge encyclopedia ch. 7), World Oral Literature Project, LL-MAP 2012, Ethnologue 16. Vitality data only; no linguistic description, no Koops manuscript listed.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Übersee 93: 287-326. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215
sources.note: Sister language only. Names Bete once, as a member of 'the whole Southern Jukunoid language group (Bezen, Bete, Lufu, Akum, Kuteb, Yukuben, Kapya)' (p. 296-297). Akum has a three-tone system (sec. 2.3); no word on stress, and nothing on Bete phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019 [PDF dated 2020]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (draft PDF from author's site; Wayback capture 2025-05-23, 198 pp.)
sources.note: Entry 46 'Bete': '3. Taraba State, Wukari LGA, Bete town. 4. Language dying out.' — no sources, references or linguistic data; classification list (p. 98) places Bete under Jukunoid: Yukuben-Kutep. Bibliography item 'Briggs, Kathleen 1972. An introductory description of the Bete language. University of Ibadan MA thesis' is cited under entry 47 Bete-Bendi (Obudu; = bete1262), not this language. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2012]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition III (draft PDF; Wayback capture 2013-04-20, 125 pp.)
sources.note: Entry 45 'Bete': Taraba State, Wukari LGA, Bete town; language dying out; unclassified. No sources. Nothing on stress.
Stubs; cite only Ethnologue, Crozier & Blench 1992, UNESCO profile, Blench 2019 Atlas and Blench 2026 Bantoid-3 paper (academia.edu, 403). No phonology.
